title: Protocol to utilize fresh uncultured human lung tumor cells for personalized functional diagnostics
protocol: Collect normal lung and tumor tissue samples.
Mechanically and enzymatically digest collected tissue samples to prepare single cell suspensions.
Label cells from lung tissue with EpCAM (CD326) antibody conjugated magnetic MicroBeads for positive selection of epithelial cells.
Fractionate cells into different types based on the presence or absence of EpCAM expression.
Test fractionated cell types for drug sensitivity and resistance.
Analyze cell viability data to identify cancer-cell selective drug vulnerabilities.
Collect tumor and tumor-adjacent normal lung tissue samples from surgically resected tumors.
Cut the tumor site in the middle and remove a 3–4 cm section of the tumor for processing.
Reserve 1–3 cm³ of tissue pieces for further analysis.
Sample normal tissue from the same lung lobe, adjacent to the tumor.
Use separate sterile scalpels for dissecting tumor and normal tissue areas.
Immediately after dissection, collect tissue pieces in 30 mL ice-cold HBSS containing antibiotics (100 U/mL penicillin, 100 mg/mL streptomycin).
Transport samples to the cell culture laboratory using a styrofoam ice box with a closed lid.
After reaching the cell culture lab, transfer tissue pieces to sterile petri plates.
Wash tissue pieces gently three times with ice-cold HBSS containing antibiotics.
Gently wash tumor tissue pieces with HBSS.
Cut the washed tumor tissue into smaller pieces for DNA, RNA, and protein analysis.
Snap freeze approximately 0.5 cm³ of tumor and normal tissue samples for DNA and protein extraction and store at -80°C.
Submerge a piece of <0.5 cm³ tissue in approximately 5× volumes of RNAlater solution at room temperature (20°C) for RNA extraction and store at -80°C.
Place >0.5 cm³ tissue samples in histo cassettes and mark the cassettes with a histology marking pen resistant to formalin, ethanol, isopropanol, and xylene for FFPE block preparation.
Reserve 1–3 cm³ of tumor tissue pieces for the FUTC assay.
Place the tissue material in a sterile petri dish.
Add 3.7 mL of ice-cold DMEM medium to the tissue.
Chop the tissue pieces as small as possible using a scalpel.
Transfer the chopped tissue pieces to the MACS C tube.
Run the preset program on the MACS dissociator designed for lung tissue dissociation.
Incubate the tissue pieces at 37°C on rotation at 50–100 rpm.
Collect the single cell suspension by straining the dissociated tissue pieces through a 70 μm cell strainer.
Centrifuge the cells to pellet them.
Discard the supernatant and resuspend the cells in fresh DMEM medium.
Remove all excess fat, fibrotic, and necrotic areas from the sample before chopping.
Cut the tissue into small 1–2 mm pieces with a sterile scalpel.
Work quickly and keep the samples cold on ice until initiating mechanical dissociation.
Mix 1 mL of DMEM with 200 μL of enzyme H, 100 μL of enzyme R, and 25 μL of enzyme A in a gentleMACS C tube.
Transfer minced tissue samples into the gentleMACS C tube containing the enzyme mix.
Close the C tube tightly and attach it upside down to a gentleMACS dissociator.
Run the gentleMACS preset ‘program h_tumor_01’ for lung tissue processing.
Detach the gentleMACS C tube from the dissociator when the spin is over.
Incubate the sample in the incubator for 30 min at 37°C under continuous rotation at 50–100 rpm.
Cool the centrifuge to 4°C after step completion.
Attach the gentleMACS C tube upside down into a gentleMACS dissociator and run the preset ‘program h_tumor_02’.
Perform a brief centrifugation step: 200 × g for 4 min at room temperature (20°C).
Resuspend the sample in the medium contained in the C tube.
Place a 70 μm cell strainer on a new 50 mL falcon tube.
Moisten the strainer surface with 5 mL DMEM.
Strain the cell suspension in the C tube through the 70 μm cell strainer.
Wash the cell strainer with 10 mL of fresh medium.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 300 × g for 7 min at room temperature (20°C).
Aspirate the supernatant completely.
Resuspend the cells in 5 mL of F-medium.
Count the number of viable cells after staining with trypan blue.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 300 × g at 4°C for 10 min.
Aspirate the supernatant completely.
Pre-cool all reagents before beginning the EpCAM+ cell enrichment.
Keep cells on ice during the procedure.
Work quickly to prevent antibody capping and non-specific labeling of cells.
Resuspend the cell pellet using cold EDTA-BSA buffer.
For 5 × 10⁷ cells, add 300 μL of EDTA-BSA buffer.
Gently pipette the suspension up and down to mix well and break up cell clumps.
Incubate the cell suspension for 30 min in the refrigerator (2°C–8°C).
After incubation is over, wash the cells by adding 10 mL of cold EDTA-BSA buffer per 5 × 10⁷ cells and centrifuge at 300 × g at 4°C for 10 min.
Assemble the column and magnetic separator during the centrifugation step.
Attach the MACS Separator to the MACS MultiStand.
Insert the MACS column into a MACS Separator, ensuring that the column's wings fit into the Separator’s notch.
Place a collection tube below the column.
Prepare the column by adding 3 mL of cold EDTA-BSA buffer to it.
Discard the flow-through and place a fresh collection tube under the column.
Aspirate the supernatant completely.
Resuspend the cell pellet using cold EDTA-BSA buffer, adding 500 μL per 108 cells.
Apply the cell suspension onto the MACS LS column and collect the flow-through containing EpCAM– cells.
Wash the column four times with 3 mL of EDTA-BSA buffer to remove any remaining unlabeled cells.
Flush out the magnetically tagged EpCAM+ cells using 5 mL of cold EDTA-BSA buffer pushed firmly into the column.
Centrifuge both the EpCAM– and EpCAM+ flow-throughs at 300 × g at 4°C for 10 min.
Aspirate and discard the supernatant completely.
Resuspend each cell pellet in 3–5 mL of F-medium.
Count the total number of cells.
Calculate the volume and cell number required for drug sensitivity testing.
Recommend usage of 384-well plates with 2,500 cells per well.
Advocate for robotic dispensing of cells and reagents.
Test each condition at least in duplicates.
Remove drug plates from storage pod.
Seed tumor-derived EpCAM+ and EpCAM– cells into two empty 384-well plates for cell viability assessment at 0 h and 72 h.
Incubate the DSRT and (72 h) viability plates for 72 h after cell seeding.
Dispense CellTiter-Glo reagent only for the 0 h viability plates.
Perform maintenance tasks involving washing and emptying MultiFlo cassettes every time the equipment is operated.
Ensure that the flow of liquid from the tip during dispensing with MultiFlo is steady and fully vertical.
Backflush with sterile Milli-Q and 70% ethanol to troubleshoot dispensing errors.
Make sure the cell suspension is homogeneous before seeding cells by pipetting up and down.
Prepare the appropriate volume of medium and reagents for two or more plates.
Place the plate on a plate shaker at 300 rpm for 5 min after cell seeding.
Incubate DSRT plates for 72 h at 37°C.
Dispense 25 μL CellTiter-Glo using MultiFlo.
Place the 0 h cell viability plate on the plate shaker at room temperature (20°C) for 5 min to induce cell lysis.
Spin the plate for 5 min at 200 × g to remove bubbles.
Record the CellTiter-Glo luminescence signal using a plate reader.
Seed EpCAM+ cells from step 36 into a 384-well plate (2,500 cells per well in 15 μL of medium).
Place the plate on a plate shaker at 300 rpm for 5 min to achieve uniform distribution of cells.
Incubate overnight (20 ± 4 h).
Add different drug concentrations on top of the cells in 10 μL of medium.
Place the plate on a plate shaker at 300 rpm for 5 min to dissolve drugs.
Incubate for 72 h and analyze viability with CellTiter-Glo as described in steps 41–44.
